| Fellow activist,

With the May 17th primary now behind us, I wanted to reach out personally to some of our more active followers who haven’t donated yet. The primary is over, but our work is far from it. We’re still working every day to register 50,000 new voters in Pennsylvania this year, and the importance of this has never been clearer. **[Fellow activist — can you step up with a quick donation of $3, $5, or $10 to help us protect our democracy?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/45812036/347593258/-1015736156?refcode=EM_FR_220527FirstDonation_N_KK_90DO_6_NG_N_L1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzkwOTIwIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ3M2Q1OTAxLWVjZGQtZWMxMS1iNjU2LTI4MTg3OGI4NTExMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zkluHX6znxLU0seeQ7T-9MMDkBQPR2i7jFQLu_qasDg=)**
[DONATE NOW](https://click.everyaction.com/k/45812037/347593259/-1015736156?refcode=EM_FR_220527FirstDonation_N_KK_90DO_6_NG_N_B1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzkwOTIwIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ3M2Q1OTAxLWVjZGQtZWMxMS1iNjU2LTI4MTg3OGI4NTExMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zkluHX6znxLU0seeQ7T-9MMDkBQPR2i7jFQLu_qasDg=) I know there’s a lot of competition for your generous contributions, so if you’re not convinced yet, I’d like to highlight a bit about what makes the New Pennsylvania Project special and why you should consider donating to us.
1. We are engaging and empowering young residents and those living in underrepresented and often neglected communities of color and immigrant communities **year-round** , canvassing, holding community and school events, and registration drives.

2. We are working with like-minded partners in these communities across Pennsylvania to expand the electorate in order to reflect our demographically changing population and make a better government that represents the values of **all Pennsylvanians**.

3. **Most of all,** we are providing education about the issues that matter in their neighborhoods and mobilizing the electorate to **vote in every election — twice a year.**

**[All that said, I hope you’ll choose now to make your first donation — we could really use it.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/45812038/347593260/-1015736156?refcode=EM_FR_220527FirstDonation_N_KK_90DO_6_NG_N_L2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzkwOTIwIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ3M2Q1OTAxLWVjZGQtZWMxMS1iNjU2LTI4MTg3OGI4NTExMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zkluHX6znxLU0seeQ7T-9MMDkBQPR2i7jFQLu_qasDg=)**
[DONATE NOW](https://click.everyaction.com/k/45812039/347593261/-1015736156?refcode=EM_FR_220527FirstDonation_N_KK_90DO_6_NG_N_B2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzkwOTIwIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ3M2Q1OTAxLWVjZGQtZWMxMS1iNjU2LTI4MTg3OGI4NTExMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zkluHX6znxLU0seeQ7T-9MMDkBQPR2i7jFQLu_qasDg=)

Kadida Kenner

_Founding Executive Director

name: Chris Constant
subject: Uvalde
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Constant for Congress
body:
| | This week, hundreds of parents dropped their children off at Robb Elementary School in Texas. The parents of 19 children will never again have the opportunity to pick up their children and ask what they learned in school. Two teachers will never have the opportunity to educate again.

This absolutely tragic event is just our latest confrontation with America’s disease of gun violence. Leaders around the country are saying there are no words to describe the tragedy in Texas. There are many words. It’s despicable, it’s unconscionable, and it’s predictable. And no other country in the world has mass shooting events with such regularity. It occurred barely one week after a gunman entered a grocery store in New York and opened fire.

I am a supporter of the Second Amendment. I myself often carry a gun for protection. But even so, it is impossible to deny something must be done. Thoughts and prayers will not fix this. This was the worst school shooting in almost a decade.

Somewhere in our history, we lost our respect for guns. We have created a culture that glamorizes guns, not for their power as a tool for safety and subsistence, but as a symbol of pop culture. Somewhere along the way we lost the culture of responsibility that used to accompany gun ownership.

I am not supportive of banning guns. As a responsible firearm owner, I am supportive of common-sense measures to limit gun violence in our society, such as red flag laws, more stringent background checks, and more strict regulation on how guns are marketed. I believe regulation is permitted by the 27 words that make up the second amendment. Unfortunately, the increasingly political U.S. Supreme Court is likely to further ratched down a state’s ability to regulate firearm safety.

Americans have vast access to guns, and too little access to mental health services, but those changes will only go so far. We need to change our relationship with guns. We cannot continue to glorify guns and gun culture, then be confounded over instances of horrific gun violence.

I fear this will not be a breaking point for our society. Gun sales will spike out of fear the president will ban guns, only exacerbating the problem. If we continue to fight over interpretations of the Second Amendment rather than waking up to the reality that we are killing each other, we will eventually go numb to the violence, if we haven’t already. Two decades ago, a single person dead in a school shooting would shock the nation. Today, it hardly makes the news.

If we don’t act now, it will be too late.

— Chris

clean_body: | | This week, hundreds of parents dropped their children off at Robb Elementary School in Texas. The parents of 19 children will never again have the opportunity to pick up their children and ask what they learned in school. Two teachers will never have the opportunity to educate again. This absolutely tragic event is just our latest confrontation with America’s disease of gun violence. Leaders around the country are saying there are no words to describe the tragedy in Texas. There are many words. It’s despicable, it’s unconscionable, and it’s predictable. And no other country in the world has mass shooting events with such regularity. It occurred barely one week after a gunman entered a grocery store in New York and opened fire. I am a supporter of the Second Amendment. I myself often carry a gun for protection. But even so, it is impossible to deny something must be done. Thoughts and prayers will not fix this. This was the worst school shooting in almost a decade. Somewhere in our history, we lost our respect for guns. We have created a culture that glamorizes guns, not for their power as a tool for safety and subsistence, but as a symbol of pop culture. Somewhere along the way we lost the culture of responsibility that used to accompany gun ownership. I am not supportive of banning guns. As a responsible firearm owner, I am supportive of common-sense measures to limit gun violence in our society, such as red flag laws, more stringent background checks, and more strict regulation on how guns are marketed. I believe regulation is permitted by the 27 words that make up the second amendment. Unfortunately, the increasingly political U.S. Supreme Court is likely to further ratched down a state’s ability to regulate firearm safety. Americans have vast access to guns, and too little access to mental health services, but those changes will only go so far. We need to change our relationship with guns. We cannot continue to glorify guns and gun culture, then be confounded over instances of horrific gun violence. I fear this will not be a breaking point for our society. Gun sales will spike out of fear the president will ban guns, only exacerbating the problem. If we continue to fight over interpretations of the Second Amendment rather than waking up to the reality that we are killing each other, we will eventually go numb to the violence, if we haven’t already. Two decades ago, a single person dead in a school shooting would shock the nation. Today, it hardly makes the news. If we don’t act now, it will be too late. — Chris | | ** Paid for by Constant for Congress Constant for Congress P.O. Box 240361 Anchorage, AK 99524 United States

| | |
---
Peter,

I’m Trudy Busch Valentine – a nurse, a mother, and a proud Missourian. [**In a moment, I’m going to ask you to become a Founding Donor to my campaign for U.S. Senate. But first, let me explain why I’m running and why your grassroots support _today_ is so critical:**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45812683/347596908/-1746441832?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk26-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NzQ4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZWNlYjczNy1lZmRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=OBFPkaSOC5f_8sqBlVecVWGfASegzquqsvFvONKRdKE=)

This year, we need to protect our razor-thin Democratic majorities in Congress. And the best defense is a good offense — so I’m proud to endorse Democrat Nikki Budzinski in Illinois’ 13th Congressional District, a key open House seat that we can flip from Republicans.

The GOP puts corporations and special interests first, but Nikki has always been a champion for working families, including helping raise the minimum wage in Illinois. Let’s flip this seat and send Nikki to Congress. name: Jessica Cisneros
subject: Can you make a contribution to our recount fund?
body:
We’re counting on our grassroots movement to power our recount.
#
Peter,
It’s Jessica Cisneros here. I just wanted to take a moment to say that I’m thankful for our movement, and [ask if you could make a split contribution to Justice Democrats and our campaign’s new recount fund?**](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/109835?refcode=em20220527-23565&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV)
We’re not backing down from the fight to count every single vote in TX-28. Henry Cuellar is the only one that has declared an outcome, but there are still vote-by-mail ballots that have yet to be counted.
We’re very much in this race, and it’s thanks to this movement that we’re so close to beating a 17-year, corporate-backed opponent. But our race is still too close to call, and we can’t take anything for granted.
To help cover the cost of the recount, we’re launching a new fund to cover the costs to make sure every vote is counted. [We’re counting on our grassroots movement to power these efforts and guarantee that the voices of all South Texans are heard. Can you split a contribution between Justice Democrats and our recount fund?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/109835?refcode=em20220527-23565&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV)
**[Contribute](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/109835?refcode=em20220527-23565&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV)**
We know that Cuellar’s corporate backers are going to spend as much money as they can on legal challenges, trying to muddy the waters and get as many of our votes thrown out as they can. And remember, Henry Cuellar is backed by the NRA, Big Oil, and the private prison industry.
We need to be ready to counter those challenges and make sure that every vote is counted and everyone’s voice is heard. **Our goal is to raise $250,000 so we have the resources we need to fully fund this recount effort.**
[Please support our recount effort by making a contribution toward our $250,000 fund goal. We’ll need all the support we can get in the next few days. ](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/109835?refcode=em20220527-23565&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV)
**[Contribute](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/109835?refcode=em20220527-23565&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=24&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV)**
Thank you so much for your support,
Jessica Cisneros

Do not worry if you cannot afford to make a contribution — we understand that this is a difficult time. If you’re struggling, you can find a food bank [here.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/28883?t=25&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV) We appreciate everything you do to keep our movement strong. Please stay informed and follow the most up-to-date recommendations from the [Centers for Disease Control](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/24438?t=26&akid=23565%2E1203867%2E7QzKEV) and your state public health department.

| Friend, With a heart overshadowed by this week’s tragedy, I still **wish to congratulate the students, parents, school faculty and staff on the work they have achieved this year.** The impact of a good teacher is immeasurable. Teachers are professionals performing an essential and difficult job that often comes with immense pressure. I hope they realize it does not go unnoticed.

While the challenges around education are present and many teachers currently have low satisfaction, [**the vast majority of Utah parents have a strongly favorable impression of their local schools and teachers.**](https://beckyforutah.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cb6d6dad27d2e4a00e5c44525&id=66983e5ec4&e=10c1db3257)

As the daughter of educators, I know the dedication and sacrifice required of teachers. I am committed to providing educators the support they need.

**Instead of asking you for a donation to our campaign today, I invite you to hug your children a little longer or send a teacher an encouraging note.**

Thank you to all who worked tirelessly to make this year a success. Thank you to teachers and staff, to community members who became substitute teachers, volunteers who rallied to support their schools, and parents who were there every step of the way.

**Have a wonderful summer break!**

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: From one devastated community to another
disclaimer_text: Paid for BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Elissa Slotkin for Congresshttps://elissaforcongress.com/ [https://elissaforcongress.com/]
Friend,
I wanted to reach out after this week’s devastating news out of Texas. A tragedy this severe is hard to process, especially as Michiganders are still reeling from the school shooting in Oxford last November.
We’ve seen firsthand the devastation that follows each of these shootings. As the representative from Oxford -- which endured a school shooting in November of last year -- I can tell you that the pain is still raw from the initial shock and disbelief. It feels like a truck is parked on your chest.
But the high school students of Oxford demonstrated a remarkable amount of courage this week despite their pain. They walked out of school to protest their leaders’ inaction on gun violence, showing more courage than many of my colleagues in the U.S. Senate and elected leaders in the Michigan legislature.
I’ve been getting calls from people across the political spectrum, including gun owners and avid hunters, who are demanding to know why we can’t put some common-sense laws in place to stop gun violence. And it’s a painful question to answer, because the answers are terrible.
In the U.S. Senate, we can’t get 10 Republicans to vote on basic solutions – things like extending background checks (which are already in place at big box stores) to internet and gun show sales, or banning bump stocks. The House has already passed *bipartisan* bills on some of these issues.
In the Michigan Senate, Republicans, including my opponent, took a party-line vote literally 24 hours after the shooting in Uvalde to reject something as simple as safe gun storage. These bills say that if you're a gun owner, you have a responsibility to reasonably secure your weapon out of reach of children. Michigan Senator Rosemary Bayer introduced that bill in the state legislature, and I introduced a similar bill at the federal level -- I am in discussions about moving it to a vote in the House now.
It’s not political to say that kids deserve to be safe in their schools and in their homes. I grew up in a gun-owning family and carried a Glock and M4 in Baghdad during my service in the CIA. The only reason to be opposed to basic solutions like safe gun storage is pure politics. It has nothing to do with protecting our children, and everything to do with politicians being scared of looking weak in front of lobbyists and their base voters.
I know I speak for all Michiganders when I say our hearts go out to the people of Uvalde: to the students, teachers, families, and the first responders whose lives have been upended. My team and I have reached out to Rep. Gonzales, Uvalde's Member of Congress, to offer our support and assistance with anything they may need, and leaders in Oxford like the fire chief and superintendent have done the same with their counterparts in Uvalde.
Everyone currently holding public office owes a meaningful solution to these grieving families. Michigan -- and our country -- deserves leaders who have the courage to do the right thing. That is what we need now more than ever.
Elissa

body:
Now that I am *officially* the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, the team and I could *really* use everyone’s help right now ...
| | |
---
Hey Peter, it’s John. I'm the official Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Pennsylvania!!!!!! 😁

We both know I don’t look like a typical politician. Maybe that’s why my tattoos are *literally* the first thing people Google about me.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814189/347602765/343689270?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=)
Well, enough Googling. Today I’ll tell you about my tattoos myself, and why I'm humbly asking for YOUR support in this race. (We're the #1 Most Likely to Flip U.S. Senate seat in the country, so we can't take it for granted!)

**On my left arm, I have the ZIP code 15104.** That’s Braddock, Pennsylvania, my home and the community I was honored to serve as mayor for 15 years. Gisele and I are raising our kids here in Braddock, right across the street from Andrew Carnegie’s first steel mill.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814190/347602766/343689270?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=)
**On my right arm I have nine different dates.** These are the dates when people were killed through violence in Braddock while I served as Mayor, starting in 2006. Seven out of nine were gun deaths. I actually have to get one more date added because in June 2018, there was another tragic loss of life. My heart breaks everytime I’m reminded of that.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814191/347602767/343689270?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=)
My first tattoo came after January 16, 2006. It was my second week on the job as mayor after winning my election by a single vote. I received a call and was summoned to a police crime scene where a pizza delivery man had been robbed and killed by gun violence.

**Every time Braddock lost someone was the worst feeling in the world, Peter.**
In a close-knit community like Braddock, it’s very likely that you know the victim and their family. It’s an incredibly wrenching and personal experience as a mayor — but nothing compared to what the families have to go through.

In my 13 years as mayor, I worked with the community to take on gun violence and other important issues that Braddock faced every day. I helped initiate youth + art programs for the students of our community and we worked together to create a community center.

We also worked to develop buildings that had been written off, kick-started our economy and reduced deadly violence. My proudest moment as mayor of Braddock is when our community went 5 1⁄2 years without the loss of life due to gun violence.

Peter, I’m running for the U.S. Senate in Pennsylvania because I believe *every* community is worth fighting for. Just like Braddock.

It is my promise to you that I'll fight for you + your community as if it were my very own.

That promise is written on my arms. Literally. ❤️
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814192/347602768/343689270?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=)
In order to build the kind of Democratic U.S. Senate campaign that can flip Pennsylvania blue + fight for every community, however, the honest truth is that we need to raise a lot of money right now. A big part of that is online activists like you chipping in when you can.

**And now that I am *officially* the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, the team and I could *really* use everyone’s help right now.**

So, I gotta ask:
**[Will you please split a donation between my campaign and Abby Finkenauer's? Every dollar helps flip these seats blue, expand our Democratic majority and send two new Democratic senators to Washington where we'll fight like hell for your community – just like we fight for ours.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814193/347602769/343689270?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=)**
| | [CONTRIBUTE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814194/347602770/343689270?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=)
---
Thanks for all you do. Together, I *know* we can win this.

Let’s gooooo. 🔥

John

John Fetterman
Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/45814195/347602771/428800054?refcode=jtk1131-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MzU5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNWM2ZjUxOC1mNGRkLWVjMTEtYjY1Ni0yODE4NzhiODUxMTAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=amvncodXzjgxF0vUKREVIzserf2jc2dgbTLA9IqOxQE=&emci=d6cf5600-a2db-ec11-b656-281878b8c32f&emdi=d5c6f518-f4dd-ec11-b656-281878b85110&ceid=13784334)

Fellow Conservative:

The Nevada Senate Republican primary is just
weeks away, and the toughest, best candidate in that race just
won the support of one of the best Governors in America.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis has endorsed Adam
Laxalt in the race to face incumbent Democrat Catherine Cortez
Masto.
"I served in the Navy with Adam," DeSantis
said, "and I can tell you that he won't back down when it comes
to standing for liberty and for what's right by our great nation.
He proved it as Nevada's attorney general, and he'll prove it
again as your next senator."
If you don't know Adam, you should. As Nevada's
Attorney General, Laxalt led on the most important issues facing
his state and our country: the right to life, energy and
environmental extremism, election integrity, and free speech.
He's running for the Senate to speak up for the
victims of woke cancel culture and to answer the bullying Left
with the only thing that can defeat them: guts.
Laxalt and DeSantis are cut from the same
cloth. They were even roommates in the Navy! Like DeSantis,
Laxalt knows the biggest threat to the country today is the elite
Left's contempt for our country and the working families who make
it great.
For her part, incumbent Democrat Catherine
Cortez Masto has spent six years in the Senate watching our
country get worse. She supports Joe Biden's inflation-inducing
spending, his open-borders disaster, and his radical, job-killing
environmental extremism.
Help flip this Senate seat with a true
conservative.
This is a clear-cut case of a freedom-loving,
principled, tough conservative taking on the Woke Elite. Laxalt
is one of the best Senate candidates in the country in 2022.
That's why Ron DeSantis made a rare endorsement outside his home
state of Florida - and it's why SCF will have his back all the
way to November and beyond.
This will be one of the tightest, meanest, most
expensive races in this election. Adam will need every dollar he
can get to fend off the attacks coming from Planned Parenthood,
the teachers' unions, and the deep state bureaucracy.
Adam Laxalt needs you.
Please join Ron DeSantis in supporting Adam

Now is the time. The primary is in June, and

Support Adam Laxalt today!

name: Ben Samuels
subject: I'm suspending my campaign. Here's why:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BEN SAMUELS FOR CONGRESS
body:
Friends,
I jumped into this race almost a year ago because of a concern for where we are headed as a country. There’s too much extremism in our politics. Too many people are willing to subvert democracy. The people who are loudest get the most attention.
People—on both sides of the aisle—feel the effect of a more divisive, more hateful, and more fractured political environment than any we’ve seen in our lifetime.
Over the past year, I have tried to bring people together: to demonstrate that we share more than we don’t, to show that collaboration and bipartisanship are still possible, to talk to Republicans, Democrats, and independents alike.
After months of deliberations, the Missouri General Assembly passed a new Congressional map two weeks ago. They did so with the explicit goal of making the Second District—the only swing district in the state—“more secure” for the incumbent Republican. They succeeded by drawing a new district that’s almost unrecognizable relative to the current district. And in the final version of the map, just like in every prior version they brought up for a vote, they drew me out of the district, always by a block or so.
In effect, the Republican state legislature has changed the rules of the game. After exhausting all of our legal options, because of how the General Assembly has gerrymandered this district, I am withdrawing from this race. We believe that this map is unconstitutional, and we will continue fighting for fair, representative elections. But that won’t change things this time around.
I would encourage you to listen to my interview this morning on St. Louis Public Radio [https://news.stlpublicradio.org/government-politics-issues/2022-05-27/citing-redistricting-changes-ben-samuels-drops-out-of-2nd-congressional-district-race] and to read my op-ed in this morning’s Washington Post. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2022/05/27/gerrymandered-out-of-missouri-district-voters-deserve-better/ ]
The fact that politicians can draw their own maps and can change the rules of the game is a huge part of the problem we face as a country. There are fewer competitive races everywhere in the United States. And it means more of the extremism and vitriol that has gotten us to where we are in the first place.
I want to say a few things to all of you, who’ve been such an integral part of my campaign:
First, the campaign may be coming to an end, but my work—our work—won’t. We will keep working to elect people who share our values and who want to make people’s lives better; we will work to recruit more diverse and younger candidates; we will work to make it easier for good and decent people to run for office. We will continue to use our platform to shine light on the fragility of democracy, and what we need to do to fix it.
Second, from the bottom of my heart, thank you. Thank you for being part of this adventure with me. Thank you for your kindness, your support, and your friendship. Thank you for believing that we can make things better. We can’t give up the fight. In the next few weeks, we will follow up with supporters individually about the next steps and ways to stay involved—for anyone who is interested, we will return your contribution (net any campaign expenses to date), and with what’s left, we will invest in and support candidates and organizations who stand up for democracy and decency in swing districts here and around the country.
Finally, I’d encourage and challenge all of you to try to close the ever-widening political gap. Reach out to someone who doesn’t vote like you—and not just on Twitter. Sit down with them for a meal or a coffee. I think you’ll find that you’ll agree on a whole lot more than you think, and you’re making it that much easier for all of us to engage with our political opponents again.
In spite of everything, it’s the people in our communities—Democrats, Republicans, and everyone else—who make me optimistic for the future.
Reach out anytime.
Onward,
Ben Samuels

name: Hakeem Jeffries
subject: Advocates like Tom Malinowski
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tom Malinowski for Congress
body:

subject: These heroes are counting on you
body:

[View this message in your browser](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2z4i0up97ebvr0a8sotskc595n2ufjg9e3vbasu8o_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h238h5e8he485he5o75pt7kkpq8ddl69qbcd1jm4qj6d9jmpqj7d9neppqcdtlmui34thgmipnadt4sbp65thhepij9c9kclgmdd1jeaqncs5mesq63cpjespnfd3hm3gr0sr6m3i32plgs6rrfkjge9h6cs5icpoe9cr3c1p36phh6aqr9ptnc9j38o5icpge1db3c3gbac9hmkorash5u)

---
Fellow American, It’s Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like _Apollo 13_ and _The Green Mile_ — but the role that changed my life, and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, was as Lt. Dan in _Forrest Gump_. **This year, I’m honored to again serve as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C.** The National Memorial Day Parade is an event like no other ... and this year, the American Veterans Center is bringing it BACK in full force, with 5,000+ participants marching down Constitution Avenue before a crowd of 250,000+ in-person, as well as T.V. broadcast that reaches 100 million households around the country. [**Fellow American, the National Memorial Day Parade is PRIMARILY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous Americans like you. Will you help chip in today to help support the Parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, or more?**](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2zdnn59ab45qtb6509vbrgoe1lbjd5edfmusseq9g_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
[**Support the National Memorial Day Parade**](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2zorgmaa50a1qoa6ehao33784sco35ig9guj22pq8_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
[](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2zg9fsqaafl6e2aiqfjhl39pbsiafbr33o4mpo5t0_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
When the American Veterans Center first called me more than 15 years ago and invited me to the National Memorial Day Parade, I was honored to join the event to remember our fallen heroes. The American Veterans Center revived the Parade in 2005 after it had been dormant for nearly 70 years. Now, in 2022, they’re bringing the Parade back to its full-scale glory after two years of pandemic precautions. Every American should be proud that generations of our brave servicemen and servicewomen, from the last of our “Greatest Generation” heroes of World War II to our veterans from Afghanistan and Iraq, will get the public thanks for their service that they deserve this year. But I know that the defenders and families of the fallen who will join me in the National Memorial Day Parade will be thinking of their friends and loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country — the brave Americans we honor on Memorial Day. **Sadly, our country is losing hundreds of World War II veterans each day, so the mission of the National Memorial Day Parade is _more important now than ever_ — as this year’s event may be the LAST opportunity for our WWII heroes to commemorate their friends who never came home.** [**Please make your most generous contribution of $25, $50, $75, $150, $250, $500, to support the National Memorial Day Parade and make it the tribute that our nation’s heroes deserve.**](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2z1sucs1bgrvrsi2e3i53is7h68srevcl3u7b74tg_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
[**Support the National Memorial Day Parade**](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2z1p8pef5edes0t5j9fl54jas5iotvd7kesmio1k0_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
The National Memorial Day Parade costs a fraction of other major public events to put on each year. In fact, _the entire parade_ costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! _That means that every dollar that’s contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event._ Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the Parade, but also supports great programs like:
* Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to Today before we lose these stories forever.
* Hold our National Youth Summit which allows young students a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, and Vietnam.
* Produce veteran focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom.

---
[](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2zbau7ivt3ru77qk87pgabd4qvj7vh6fkeqlu6au0_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
[**Please join me in support of the National Memorial Day Parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, $250, $500, or more right now.**](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2zfniq7gulhql3s3fkbh0bq8sc0rte8hr2ljf3i60_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs) But no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you.

On Memorial Day — this year and every year — please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in D.C. Visit a local veterans’ cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. _I believe we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, but we can always do a little more._ Fellow American, thank you for your support of America's heroes, and please — [**if you're able, make a gift to help fund the National Memorial Day Parade right now.**](http://e.americandefensenews.com/rd/9z2zcblll0c01cmfg5e2ilvpha8nnodflchn5iibsk8_rp22sh2s8i66pb6cdjm9o72c1h2bs)
---
Sincerely,

Gary Sinise
Honorary Grand Marshal
National Memorial Day Parade

You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile — but the role that changed my life, and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, was as Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump. This year, I’m honored to again serve as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. The National Memorial Day Parade is an event like no other ... and this year, the American Veterans Center is bringing it BACK in full force, with 5,000+ participants marching down Constitution Avenue before a crowd of 250,000+ in-person, as well as T.V. broadcast that reaches 100 million households around the country. When the American Veterans Center first called me more than 15 years ago and invited me to the National Memorial Day Parade, I was honored to join the event to remember our fallen heroes. The American Veterans Center revived the Parade in 2005 after it had been dormant for nearly 70 years. Now, in 2022, they’re bringing the Parade back to its full-scale glory after two years of pandemic precautions. Every American should be proud that generations of our brave servicemen and servicewomen, from the last of our “Greatest Generation” heroes of World War II to our veterans from Afghanistan and Iraq, will get the public thanks for their service that they deserve this year. But I know that the defenders and families of the fallen who will join me in the National Memorial Day Parade will be thinking of their friends and loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country — the brave Americans we honor on Memorial Day. Sadly, our country is losing hundreds of World War II veterans each day, so the mission of the National Memorial Day Parade is more important now than ever — as this year’s event may be the LAST opportunity for our WWII heroes to commemorate their friends who never came home. The National Memorial Day Parade costs a fraction of other major public events to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that’s contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the Parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to Today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our National Youth Summit which allows young students a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, and Vietnam. * Produce veteran focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day — this year and every year — please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in D.C. Visit a local veterans’ cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, but we can always do a little more. body:
Four years ago, weeks after the second deadliest school shooting in modern American history in Parkland, Florida, Donald Trump spoke at the NRA Convention.
#

Friends --
Four years ago, weeks after the second deadliest school shooting in modern American history in Parkland, Florida, Donald Trump spoke at the NRA Convention.
He got on stage and said that giving teachers concealed weapons was the best way to stop the epidemic of school shootings in America.
Today, he returns to the NRA Convention, speaking sometime this afternoon. And before he takes the stage, there’s a fact you need to know:
Guns are the number one cause of death of kids in America today. Guns. Not accidents. Not car crashes. Not anything else. Guns.
We know that keeping guns away from domestic abusers would change that. We know safe storage laws would change that. We know extreme risk protection orders (aka red flag laws) would change that.
Arming teachers would only mean more kids shot at school, not fewer. The chance of an accident, miscalculation, or a crisis increases exponentially.
This has been a tough week—no doubt—and it will be hard to watch Trump speak today. But it will be a clear illustration of what we are up against: a far-right committed to the profits of gun manufacturers above all else. Gun extremists who believe that guns being the leading cause of death for kids is just the cost of doing business.
But we can fight back. And we will win. And we must, because winning means saving lives. But Gabby cannot do it alone:

Elissa Slotkin tried to knock Tom off the ballot with a frivolous challenge to his address - not his residency - his address. a The board of Canvassers rejected Slotkin’s challenge by a unanimous 4-0 vote. Tom is _officially_ the Republican candidate for Congress!

#### **Pain at the Pump**
Gas prices in Michigan continue to increase causing Michiganders to feel the weight as more of their take-home income gets gobbled up on basic necessities. Joe Biden and Elissa Slotkin based their campaign on making things better for Americans but whether it is gas prices, inflation, the economy, baby formula...things are much, much worse. Elissa Slotkin has [voted with Joe Biden 100% of the time](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6290f5952b10a617f72fc1b6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fprojects.fivethirtyeight.com%2Fbiden-congress-votes%2Felissa-slotkin%2F&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&l=en-US&s=DjIwt0jf8UFs56roI1eQWzBDcbE%3D) and in November, we have the opportunity to hold her accountable.See more[ here](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6290f5952b10a617f72fc1b6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fbarrettbrigade1%2Fposts%2F455468083054270&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&l=en-US&s=hquQePSAXs9Y-zRzXcqG5-og2q4%3D).

#### **Biden Administration Opening Southern Border**
This past Monday, Title 42 expired, a Trump policy that allows the U.S. to return illegal immigrants to their home country if they pose a health risk to the U.S. The Biden Administration has vowed to end the policy, however a federal judge intervened to stop this disastrous change. The Administration’s decision is expected to increase illegal immigration to as many as **one million people each month.** Elissa Slotkin, Biden’s top ally in Michigan, has voted with the Administration lock-step on immigration policy, [earning her an F-](https://mgcp02.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6290f5952b10a617f72fc1b6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.numbersusa.com%2Fcontent%2Fmy%2Fcongress%2F19335%2Fgradescoresheet%2F&w=618846223a022e7ecb41d30c&l=en-US&s=JtUu30vbo3EoDht2tl9ljAsXBAE%3D) from immigration reform group NumbersUSA.Rep. Slotkin has different priorities than the people she represents.

You may know me from my roles in movies like _Apollo 13_ and _The Green Mile_ — but the role that changed my life, and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, was as Lt. When the American Veterans Center first called me more than 15 years ago and invited me to the National Memorial Day Parade, I was honored to join the event to remember our fallen heroes. The American Veterans Center revived the Parade in 2005 after it had been dormant for nearly 70 years. Now, in 2022, they’re bringing the Parade back to its full-scale glory after two years of pandemic precautions. Every American should be proud that generations of our brave servicemen and servicewomen, from the last of our “Greatest Generation” heroes of World War II to our veterans from Afghanistan and Iraq, will get the public thanks for their service that they deserve this year. But I know that the defenders and families of the fallen who will join me in the National Memorial Day Parade will be thinking of their friends and loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country — the brave Americans we honor on Memorial Day. **Sadly, our country is losing hundreds of World War II veterans each day, so the mission of the National Memorial Day Parade is _more important now than ever_ — as this year’s event may be the LAST opportunity for our WWII heroes to commemorate their friends who never came home.** [**Please make your most generous contribution of $25, $50, $75, $150, $250, $500, to support the National Memorial Day Parade and make it the tribute that our nation’s heroes deserve.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=67b06189db7c4e0ebb85f52941ca2fe5&_e=Ul-S2bAcgGd4356_pwHOjM0KMTb6hdIn_dnjM9t2xP9L3IrrSS_W6VeeYTBkpozSgLb5Vy0USJJJRwGmct8VhMr5BRZpONvQEZ_qlI45Pz4fxKCRS4Dw-cy2o03oDBm2M9dli5N2apWD7aaQKYbTRTpy0EJTnoRNj7n6gT-VsUqHz-tezOBjiRj5iOKmSlmioWlU--tnKfTshmgSYhMUJ3nHSNvYUb2VdPRGAu7R9UKnkoEI0V0lR6yP2PjxTk02fNPMB4RnRphotLhs7pjHpo8HVSRDgRsKFQjJjIiM7z1NiOf17LGdXKlA1kU5ZObvFhP0oiff_OfzpQobmaGOYBNlEePJavwjKI63yApYMSk%3D)

The National Memorial Day Parade costs a fraction of other major public events to put on each year. In fact, _the entire parade_ costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! _That means that every dollar that’s contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event._ Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the Parade, but also supports great programs like:
* Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to Today before we lose these stories forever.
* Hold our National Youth Summit which allows young students a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, and Vietnam.
* Produce veteran focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom.

Patriot,

I'd like to share my personal story with you. In the 1970s, my mother became pregnant with me. She was in her early 20's, had no college education, and wasn't married. At the time, having children at such a young age and out of wedlock was extremely out of the norm, let alone accepted.

What was meant to be one of the most joyful moments in her life, also became one of the most difficult, she received extreme pressure from those around her to have an abortion.

By the grace of God, my mother moved forward with her pregnancy, fully knowing how her life might change. As a single mother, she fully relied on God and the support of loved ones to help raise me.

Today I stand here having lived a full life, and I am grateful for my mother's decision.

Although we didn't see it then, the adversity my mother and I faced together led me to where I am today.

Arizona deserves a representative that will actually fight for the things that matter, = | = Time and time again, we’ve seen how out-of-touch our leaders in Congress are. David Schweikert has a track record of working against the people of this district – from opposing bills that would lower the cost of insulin to undermining our democracy. I’m ready to get in there and fight for things that will actually help the people of Arizona. Healthcare costs are too high, income inequality has run rampant for far too long, and climate change is occurring at an alarming rate. I was wondering if you had a couple minutes to help me with something today.

It feels like with this new administration in power, anything is possible. Donald J. Trump May 26th, 2022
President Donald J. Trump, 45th President of the United States of America, will be joined by endorsed candidate for Wyoming’s At-Large Congressional District, Harriet Hageman, members of the United States House of Representatives, and other special guests on Saturday, May 28, 2022, in Casper, WY.

This Save America rally is a continuation of President Trump’s unprecedented effort to advance the MAGA agenda by energizing voters and highlighting America First candidates and causes.

President Donald J. Trump, 45th President of the United States of America, Delivers Remarks

Ford Wyoming Center
1 Events Drive
Casper, WY 82601

Rep. Andy Biggs, _U.S. Representative for Arizona’s 5th Congressional District_

* Fighting to **lower costs** on things folks rely on every day, from gas, to groceries, to prescription drugs.
* Pushing to **bring manufacturing jobs back** to Michigan, and fix our supply chains so we can make more things in America, not China.
* Building on the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law by bringing home more resources to **replace lead pipes, fix our roads, and get more families broadband access.**
* Standing up to defend _Roe v. Wade_ and **make sure the freedom to choose is protected** for people in Michigan and beyond.

I’m fighting to move these issues forward and make life better for mid-Michigan families every single day in Congress.

**But I’m up against tough odds in my re-election battle for the midterms — because my opponents and their dark money backers are dumping in money to try to flip this seat.**

subject: Cuts to my core

body:
Peter , I am not asking you to chip in or to add your name. I want to ask you a simple question.

What is a child’s life worth to you?

Ask Senator Ted Cruz and he should say $442,000.

Ask Senator John Cornyn and he should say $340,000.

Ask our very own Senator Ron Johnson and he should say $223,000.

(Source: https://www.axios.com/2022/05/25/ted-cruz-lawmakers-money-gun-rights-groupshttps://www.axios.com/2022/05/25/ted-cruz-lawmakers-money-gun-rights-groups)

These are the contributions that these three spineless Senators received from gun rights groups to stop common-sense gun laws like the Enhanced Background Checks Act and the Bipartisan Background Checks Act that we passed in the House and sent to the Senate well over a year ago.

I am devastated. Not just about the mass shootings, but the horrific increase in gun violence. Please know that I will continue doing everything I can to pass common sense gun laws and I am calling on my Republican colleagues in the House and Senate to start doing the same.

We can build a world where our kids can go to school, go to church, and live freely as children without the fear of gun violence. Shootings don’t have to continue being a daily occurrence and we can never allow these tragedies to be the norm.

Come November we can help make this a reality and build a brighter future for our children.

In solidarity,
-Gwen
Proudly representing Wisconsin's Fourth Congressional District
Proud Co-Lead of the Violence Against Women Act

subject: The NRA convention starts today
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY NEWSOM FOR CALIFORNIA – GOVERNOR – 2022
body:
Their vision for America — a country where everyone is armed to the teeth at times, no training necessary and no permit required.

Friends -
Earlier this morning, just a couple hours away from the Ross Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, the NRA kicked off its annual convention.
It starts with what they call a “wall of guns” where attendees can win one of dozens of weapons on display.
Donald Trump is speaking.
Wayne LaPierre will speak, as well.
And if history is any guide, they are going to continue to peddle the fantasy that all we need to make our communities safer from gun violence is... guns everywhere.
That is their vision for America — a country where everyone is armed to the teeth at all times, no training necessary, and no permit required.
But it’s not just Donald Trump and Wayne LaPierre:
Daniel Defense, the manufacturer of the weapon used in Uvalde earlier this week has a large presence at the convention. They host an exhibit and are sponsors of two large events, including one with a former member of the now-defunct NRA TV.
We share this to say that Donald Trump, Wayne LaPierre, Daniel Defense and the 636 exhibitors selling weapons, ammunition, tactical gear and more at the convention will do everything they can to stop Gavin Newsom from signing legislation that will make our California communities safer from gun violence.
They will try to derail our bills.

--Elie Mystal, MSNBC_

name: Abigail Spanberger
subject: Protecting kids and our communities - what can be done
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Spanberger for Congress
body:
| Peter,

I write with a deep sadness but renewed resolve, and I hope you will take the time to read this email and commit [or recommit] to advocating for change. Year after year and shooting after shooting, there are always calls to "not get political" as we mourn our fellow Americans.

But everything is political, including how we keep our kids safe in school, because the policies and laws that govern our communities, states, and country are decided by the people we elect. And as community member after community member reaches out to me desperately asking what can be done, **let me tell you about some of the straightforward policies I support and why.**

**Raise the age to purchase assault-style weapons:** Per federal law, you must be 21 to purchase a handgun, but you can buy an assault-style weapon like an AR-15 at 18. We must raise the age to 21.

**Reinstate a ban on large-capacity magazines: **The data clearly show that large-capacity magazines make shootings significantly more lethal because murderers can shoot more rounds faster.

**Put Extreme Risk Protective Order (ERPO) legislation in place:** Ensure that law enforcement can take action when they receive reports from family or friends that someone might be a harm to themselves or others.

**Require Background Checks on all sales:** Per federal law, some people with a history of violence are prohibited from purchasing firearms. To ensure these "prohibited buyers" can't buy a firearm, would-be purchasers must fill out a background check form. However, federal law only requires a background check at federally-licensed points of sale, which means in many states, online sales or gun show sales do not require a background check!

The House of Representatives has twice voted to ensure the law is enforced across all points of sale with **H.R. 8, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act.** The legislation passed the House with the support of eight Republicans who value this common-sense law. It awaits a vote in the Senate.

**Close the Charleston Loophole: **Per federal law, gun purchases may occur by default after three business days -- even if a background check has not been returned. Though 90% of federal background checks are completed in minutes, the ones that take longer are four times more likely to be denied, and this means the three-day default results in guns being sold to prohibited buyers, including the man who murdered congregants of Emanuel AME Church in Charleston, SC. **H.R. 1446 Enhanced Background Checks Act of 2021** would lengthen the default period from three days to 10. This bill passed the House with bipartisan support and awaits a vote in the Senate.

**If you want to learn more about these issues or get engaged in local advocacy,** take a look at the following organizations. They have local chapters and whether you're a parent, a gun owner, a student, or simply concerned about this issue, there is a place for you!

| | | Hi Peter,

I'm emailing you to remind you that May is Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month. Every May since 1992, we celebrate the great and many contributions of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders to the fabric of our nation.

We should also be reminded of the importance of standing in solidarity with our AAPI neighbors in the fight against Asian hate. We were born as a nation of immigrants and diversity makes us stronger and enriches our personal experiences and communities.

You can be sure that in Congress I’ll continue my lifelong efforts to uplift the experiences of AAPI communities and won’t rest until all voices are heard, just as I have done throughout my career as a council member, mayor, and Assembly Speaker pro Tem.

That’s why I’m so proud to be endorsed by a broad coalition of AAPI leaders across our district and state, including State Treasurer Fiona Ma, Assemblymember Phil Ting, Assemblymember Alex Lee, and Assemblymember Evan Low, San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu, San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan, and San Francisco Police Commissioner and President of the Hop Wo Benevolent Association Larry Yee, and many others.

I hope that this AAPI Heritage Month is filled with pride, reflection, and action.

Best,

Kevin Mullin

subject: I wish I didn’t have to write this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jared Moskowitz for Congress
body:
Dear Friends,

When my daughter Jaime was murdered in the Parkland shooting four years ago, I was heartbroken and devastated. I still am.

Jared Moskowitz is the person that fought for me and the other Parkland parents in the aftermath of the shooting.

Jared led the fight to pass historic gun violence prevention legislation in Florida. His singular mission was to try and prevent another tragedy like the shooting that took Jaime from us.

Nothing can bring my daughter back, but Jared worked to honor her memory by preventing other families from feeling the same pain. That’s why I’m supporting him to represent us in Congress.

The shooting in Uvalde, Texas was incredibly painful to watch. It brought my heart and mind right back to February 14, 2018, the day my daughter was murdered.

The horrific shooting in Texas was preventable. The shooter purchased guns on his 18th birthday. In Florida, he wouldn’t have been able to because thanks to Jared, the minimum age to purchase a gun
here is 21.

This week proved yet again that we need federal gun violence prevention legislation, and we need it now.

I’m supporting Jared Moskowitz because no one is more qualified–and no one will do more–to get this done. If he can pass gun violence prevention legislation in Republican-controlled Tallahassee, I know Jared can pass it in Washington.

When my beautiful daughter, Jaime, was shot and killed, my wife was working at a preschool where Jared’s son was in class. She put Jared’s 4-year old son in a closet to keep him safe.

Less than a month later, Jared told this story on the Florida House floor and passed gun violence prevention legislation in Tallahassee. It didn’t ease the pain of Jaime’s murder, and neither will federal
legislation in the wake of Uvalde, but it will accomplish our goal: preventing another devastating tragedy.

Please join me in the fight against gun violence by supporting Jared Moskowitz for Congress.

Thank you,

Fred

name: Ralph Rebandt For Governor
subject: Candidate Rebandt Calls for Day of Prayer
body:
PRESS RELEASE-Five candidates have been denied the opportunity to run for Governor of the great state of Michigan.

| [ ](http://www.ralphrebandtforgovernor.com/?e=35c30c37841d37cfa9d73635bc93e640&utm_source=ralphrebandtforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=5_candidates_out&n=1)
---
**PRESS RELEASE**

Five candidates have been denied the opportunity to run for Governor of the great state of Michigan. I express my sincere regret to these patriots who rose to stand up to the corrupt and disastrous Whitmer Administration at tremendous personal cost. I want to thank them personally for their sacrifice and for their desire to seek a better future for Michigan.

Today is not a day to rejoice in their loss, but rather a day to unite around our common goal, and to fight our common enemy. The globalist agenda is working to divide us. I will take leadership in our party to assure that they are not successful.

The fact remains that although the signatures were not eligible, it does not speak to the character or heart of these candidates. I will not allow the liberals to run this narrative. I will run this narrative. I firmly stand behind these candidates and support their efforts to investigate the evil that has taken place. When evil wins, we all lose. Therefore, I am calling on the citizens of Michigan to make this coming **Tuesday, May 31st** ,**a day of prayer to Almighty God** , asking that the entangled web of evil at all levels in our political process, be exposed and that we will be led back to**truth, respect, dignity, and love for one another.**

Our campaign has seen exponential growth in the past few weeks and I believe it is because we value these four principles. Republicans, conservatives, grass-root patriots, as well as Democrats are uniting with us because they are attracted to our vision to**“Make Michigan a Lighthouse to the Nation.”** support.
## **SUPPORT THE CAMPAIGN**
Things are gearing up as we get closer to the primary on August 2nd. We need **YOUR** support in order to defeat Whitmer and **Make Michigan A Lighthouse To The Nation.** Sign up on our website to volunteer or donate to help the campaign.

But the reality is we can’t get any of these things done if we don’t keep Vermont and the Senate blue.

_**"I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [Herschel Walker and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."**
--Elie Mystal, MSNBC_

Peter,

I recently wrote to you about a racist article attacking me in _The Nation_.

The author had some pretty heinous things to say because I'm a Black conservative. You may recall this line:

_"Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people."_
Well, Peter, he's back at it again. MSNBC featured this man on their network this week so he could spew even more anti-Black, anti-conservative vitriol in the name of mediocre TV ratings.

He doubled down in his attacks on me. This time he attacked Republican Senator Tim Scott (SC) too. Here's part of what he said:

_"I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [referring to me and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."_
**That's racist, disgusting, and sad.**

I never wanted the color of my skin to be a focal point of this Senate campaign, but these attacks on my character and my skin color have gone too far.

**You can help me prove them wrong by standing with me at this critical moment.**

We'd like to show them a groundswell of grassroots support from across Georgia and around the country. **[Can I count on you to help me today?](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=534d41537005411ca290498145e6cf8d&_e=YMnxJUCry1XZ4eukIgZugZrsYJmzi9rTxcGQs0D6Pu51n7jVAW7UZFoKbI5vsh-3EIz2UmkO_6qVyIqtOkBWZQmd3AcuEOTFVi9YYkAqpH7o9stwcawPqWhvwUlkmfCoUysmZdmlB9dp6CAaOtYtO1zYipwbTtQijDjPEH4GyTT-hqpJykLlIqfwV7rsDtqbcALfC2VCkBvvUQ2dLEh9bxWdyQpTGW6RdyZes47KTY2RVfUw10r45_jcbf59uNUAqE-vy7ZjTnTbqzwu1gWbz-HpkbmOYfb26QA-AYslKKu3BOmJtdjVBOFoKDLhXCrFNcVf4tnNEXA0tyf9jCBcOJR0NaxtyJPqJPpZ-lTucHboeTzwBomsBexScbXLKq_JwtY8Urx5DcHkXUgTVv84FTKQz9SskTX5lypSJ8AeGB_PAgk-lkxTJJewi4xsBtghITCBhwo2A95_nUtf9_1Flv3Ez49tFDIqNfHeWwxp8v42Z4N57KRHOfCLnfGH6k55)**

_Just imagine if these comments were made by a conservative about a Black Democrat. They'd be fired immediately after going off air._

**I won't be quiet about this.** This columnist is saying horrible things about fellow human beings based on the color of their skin. That's simply wrong.

| Friend,My name is Colonel Roger Lintz, and I've had the honor of knowing Bryce Reeves for over 30 years. In this crucial election on June 21st, we need to make sure we pick someone that we trust, and I'm asking you to make that person Bryce Reeves. As his commanding officer for nearly two years in the early 90s, Bryce was my second-in-command. His integrity and his honor were of the highest order, and I had 100% confidence in Bryce to lead in my absence. It was a pleasure to serve our country with him. But more than his leadership and integrity, the highest compliment I can give him is this: he is a loyal man of his word, and I know when he says something he means it.

name: =?utf-8?Q?Tracey=20Mann?=
subject: Kansas Farm Bureau Endorsement
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Mann for Congress, Inc
body:
Kansas Farm Bureau's endorsement is the gold standard in the Big First... | | |
---
| |
---
| Friends,

This week our campaign was endorsed once again by the Kansas Farm Bureau, as we were two years ago when I first ran for Congress. The Kansas Farm Bureau's endorsement is the gold standard in the Big First because it represents grassroots support from ag producers at the county level who make up the vast majority of the KFB organization throughout the First District.

I am honored to have this endorsement because KFB members are my neighbors, friends, and family; they are the local leaders who understand the needs and concerns of Kansas farmers, ranchers, and agricultural producers. I am grateful for their support as I continue to advocate for agriculture and our Kansas conservative values.

Agriculture is in my blood. I’m a fifth generation Kansan, and I grew up in a house that my great-great-grandfather ordered from a Montgomery Ward catalogue in the early 1900s on a farm that my parents and brother still operate. Some of my fondest memories from childhood are working cattle with my grandfather, father, and brother on the family feed yard where I learned the most valuable lessons of life: faith, love of neighbor, hard work, and responsibility.

Kansas Farm Bureau’s endorsement is truly humbling. I did not come to Congress to be a caretaker in the slow demise of America. I came to defend agriculture, Kansas conservative values, and work to make our country stronger. That’s my responsibility as your representative, and I am grateful for the support from the Kansas Farm Bureau as I seek a second term in Congress to continue serving the great people of the Big First.

Sincerely,

Tracey Mann

P.S. clean_body: Kansas Farm Bureau's endorsement is the gold standard in the Big First... | | | | | | Friends, This week our campaign was endorsed once again by the Kansas Farm Bureau, as we were two years ago when I first ran for Congress. The Kansas Farm Bureau's endorsement is the gold standard in the Big First because it represents grassroots support from ag producers at the county level who make up the vast majority of the KFB organization throughout the First District. I am honored to have this endorsement because KFB members are my neighbors, friends, and family; they are the local leaders who understand the needs and concerns of Kansas farmers, ranchers, and agricultural producers. I am grateful for their support as I continue to advocate for agriculture and our Kansas conservative values. Agriculture is in my blood. I’m a fifth generation Kansan, and I grew up in a house that my great-great-grandfather ordered from a Montgomery Ward catalogue in the early 1900s on a farm that my parents and brother still operate. Some of my fondest memories from childhood are working cattle with my grandfather, father, and brother on the family feed yard where I learned the most valuable lessons of life: faith, love of neighbor, hard work, and responsibility. Kansas Farm Bureau’s endorsement is truly humbling. I did not come to Congress to be a caretaker in the slow demise of America. I came to defend agriculture, Kansas conservative values, and work to make our country stronger. That’s my responsibility as your representative, and I am grateful for the support from the Kansas Farm Bureau as I seek a second term in Congress to continue serving the great people of the Big First. Sincerely, Tracey Mann P.S. subject: Fighting for our children is as important as ever
body:
Hear what Courtney has to say | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/1f725b58eedd/fighting-for-our-children-is-as-important-as-ever?e=20ac8f046f)
---
| |
---
| | Dear Peter, [On Tuesday, May 24, a gunman entered Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, TX and gunned down nineteen 4th graders and two teachers.](https://courtneygeelsforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0ca724a68d4210b231de53e89&id=bc5bf2c1c8&e=20ac8f046f)
---
|
---
| That murderer committed a despicable act of evil because he was an evil person. I don't know his motives; I don't know his past trauma; I don't know anything about him. But I know that we call people evil because they do evil things. The root cause of this and other massacres like it is that humans are unfortunately capable of doing horrible things. Was he demented? Probably. Did he have a difficult upbringing that led to deep-seated psychological issues? To be sure. But make no mistake: he was evil. And though that awful man used an AR-15 to commit this atrocity, I'm blaming him because he is responsible. That AR-15 didn't have agency; he did.

Now please don't misunderstand me...I don't want to politicize this like the Democrats have by bringing up guns, or the 2nd amendment, or whatever else they'd like to blame for this evil. I speak of blame. I blame him, not the tool he used. And when we blame the tool and not the human who wielded it, we siphon off some of the blame and in part absolve him of what he is 100% responsible for.

If they want to have a conversation about gun regulations, we can do that. Our country thrives on good, productive dialogue. I'm 100% for the 2nd amendment and I will defend everyone's Right to Bear Arms because I believe when good, responsible Americans wield weapons, they act as a deterrence to the murder of innocent children. They disagree and that's their prerogative.

But I am sick and tired of the politicization of tragedy that makes guns responsible for what a homicidal, despicable, pathetic man-child did. The Democrats seem to want to scapegoat evil with partisan gun talking points to preserve their ill-conceived belief in progress. We don't blame cars for drunk driving deaths. Why on earth would we blame the tool for the deaths of our children? Until we address the evil at the root of these heinous crimes by addressing the ethical rot that's plagued our society, no amount of regulation will stop the suffering of innocents. '

Please be in prayer for the victims and their families. They did not deserve this. Let's strive to be better and invest in building up our children.
---
|
---
| _One small thing we can do as a down-payment for the future is invest in the lives of the children around us. The Boys and Girls club desires "to combat the growing juvenile delinquency problem in the community and ensure that all Club members are on track to graduate from high school with a plan for the future." **Will you please consider making a donation to this wonderful nonprofit?**_
---
|
---
| _Contributions made to the Boys and Girls Club **ARE tax-deductible**, and **ALL of this money will go directly to the Boys and Girls Club of Durham**. Courtney Geels for Congress will purchase pizza for the children on June 7th. **Please join me there at 4pm on June 7th wearing your Courtney Geels for Congress shirt and help me distribute pizza with our collective monetary gift**.

Please write checks to "**Boys & Girls Clubs of Durham and Orange Counties**." You can mail the check to my PO Box at: **PO Box 995, Hillsborough, NC 27278**. It would be amazing to present a large blessing to these hardworking staffers and show they have the support of our team and of Republicans in our community. If you would like to join me on June 7th, please indicate that in the volunteer link below._
---
| [Volunteer](https://courtneygeelsforcongress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0ca724a68d4210b231de53e89&id=b5f75ec84d&e=20ac8f046f "Volunteer")
---
| Peter, we have a big fight ahead of us to flip this seat RED in November. Let's make sure we make a splash at the Boys and Girls Club on June 7. Thank you for supporting my campaign.

Warmest regards.
---
| |
---
---
| Courtney Geels

name: Gisele Barreto Fetterman
subject: Hi, I’m the SLOP!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fetterman for PA
body:
This is a longer email from me, but I hope you read it
#
Hi Derek,
Our campaign has grown quickly over the past week since John won the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, but I wanted to take a minute to introduce myself, in case we haven’t met yet.
I’m Gisele Barreto Fetterman, the Second Lady of Pennsylvania. Or, as I like to call myself, the SLOP. 😂
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220527-1?refcode=em20220527-6010&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)
_Here I am on Election Night filling in for João._
This is the story of me and John — but it gets a little long. **[If you don’t have the time to read this all right now, please consider making a donation of any amount towards our campaign today. No amount is too little to make a difference.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220527-1?refcode=em20220527-6010&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)**
I met John many years, three kids, and two dogs ago — before he was Pennsylvania’s next senator. Back then, he was just a guy trying to pour love into Braddock, a small steel town that helped build America, but had been left behind. He moved there to teach GED classes, and after two of his students were gunned down, he ran for mayor to stop the violence and bring back jobs.
I read about the work John was doing, and I was inspired. Long story short? I joined him in Braddock, he fell madly in love with me, we got married, and we’ve been working together ever since to make sure no one is left behind.
But really, though. I immigrated to this country with my mom when I was just a kid. I was a DREAMer. And when our son August heard that, he asked me: “Mommy, what did you dream about?” 😭
I told him: I dreamt about him. And that was true. But also, **I dreamt about all of this.**
Like so many others, I found the American dream, and made my life in Western Pennsylvania. I found love, a wonderful family, and a place I am proud to raise my children. **John and I want to make sure that everyone in Pennsylvania can find the American dream here, too.**
On the surface, John and I don’t seem like we’d have a lot in common. (According to the zodiac we are only 11% compatible — of course I checked!)
But what connected us then — and what connects us now — is a shared conviction: **no person should be left behind, and no community should be forgotten.**
John has always stood out. My grandmother Bibi used to say he had to be made that tall because it was the only way to fit his whole heart. ❤️
But it’s not just his height, his goatee, or his refusal to wear long pants — even when I beg him to — that make him different. It’s not just because John looks nothing like a politician (and is deliriously handsome, but don’t tell him I said that).
It’s because John doesn’t _act_ like a politician. At heart, he's still that hardworking, scrappy, small-town mayor. He wants to know the people he’s serving. He feels a responsibility to each and every one of them. And he fights for people like he’d fight for a neighbor, like he’d fight for our family.
**That is what makes John different. And that is what makes him tough enough to fight for Pennsylvania.**
He did it in Braddock. He did it in Harrisburg. And now, he’s going to do the same thing in Washington.
Now, I’m going to be honest with you. Politics is mean — and I’m not. But the truth is, too many people in this commonwealth and this country are hurting. Too many people feel abandoned and ignored. Too many people think their best days are behind them. Nothing is more cruel than the feeling of being hopeless.
But John has a plan and a purpose to make sure Pennsylvania’s best days are ahead of us.
He’s going to fight for abortion rights.
He’s going to fight to raise the minimum wage and protect the union way of life.
He’s going to fight to protect our planet.
He’s going to fight to eliminate the filibuster.
He’s going to fight to legalize cannabis.
He’s going to fight against gun violence.
He’s going to fight against inflation and corporate greed.
And he’s going to fight so this country starts making things in America again — the way it once did in Braddock.
Of course, the general election is less than six months away. And because Pennsylvania is our #1 chance to pick up a Democratic seat in the Senate, this race will likely be the biggest, most competitive, and most watched race in the country. (It’s already the most expensive! 🤯)
_But it might also be the nastiest._
Now that John’s officially the Democratic nominee, there’s going to be more dark money, more negative ads, more lies spread about him than most of us can imagine.
It could even start tomorrow.
Fortunately, John is up to the challenge. But he can’t do it alone.
**He needs your help to fight back.**
**[So please, if you can, please make a donation of any amount today to support John’s campaign for U.S. Senate. John has always had our backs — now it’s time we have his.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220527-1?refcode=em20220527-6010&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220527-1?amount=5&refcode=em20220527-6010&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)**
This race we’re running — it’s a race for the future of every community across Pennsylvania. For every small town, for every person who calls those small towns home, and for every person who’s considered leaving because they just didn’t see enough opportunities.
It’s a race for every job that’s been lost, for every factory that’s been closed, for every cost that keeps rising, and every worker who can’t keep up.
It’s a race for a better Pennsylvania, a better country.
And it’s a race that, together, we will win in November!
Thank you for taking the time to read this. Your support means the world to me, John, our family, and this whole campaign.
With love and gratitude,
Gisele ❤️
Gisele Barreto Fetterman
Second Lady of Pennsylvania (SLoP)
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220527-1?refcode=em20220527-6010&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)
P.S. **[There is still time to become a Founding Donor to this campaign. Don’t miss your chance to say you were a proud supporter of this campaign from the very beginning by making a donation today.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220527-1?refcode=em20220527-6010&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)**

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-emails?refcode=em20220527-6010-footer&t=1&refcode2=6010_434096_TmaeTB&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)**
---
[](https://www.facebook.com/JohnFettermanPA/) | [](https://twitter.com/johnfetterman) | [](https://www.instagram.com/johnfetterman/)
Email us: info@johnfetterman.com
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end. Small donors like you keep us going. To contribute via check, please address to Fetterman for PA, PO Box 6061, Pittsburgh PA 15211.
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.johnfetterman.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/)
* [Update My Personal Information](https://act.johnfetterman.com/sign/personal_info/?t=2&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)
* [Unsubscribe](https://act.johnfetterman.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=6010%2E434096%2ETmaeTB)

| | | Hi there, Did you know that 120,000 kids are homeless? Or that 40,000 veterans are homeless? That’s what I emphasized when I went on Fox News primetime with Jesse Watters last night. Fox has been attacking my ideas for weeks now, but even Watters had to agree that in the richest country on Earth, no one should be homeless — especially not kids and veterans. I’ve even gotten emails from Fox viewers who said they’re not Democrats — including one person who’s a combat vet — who told me they liked my ideas for increasing the minimum wage and using vacant homes for housing.
