clean_body: Thank you for your generous support of Tom's campaign! Keep reading for a recap of his time on the campaign trail, an update on upcoming events, and ways to get involved. Team Tom Weekly Update | Friday, May 27th, 2022 Peter, Last week our #MomenTOM grew even stronger with two major endorsements — the Maryland State AFL-CIO and The Washington Post! We are so excited as these most recent endorsements represent people across the state and prove to us that when people learn more about Tom’s track record of getting things done, they support him. Our broad, diverse coalition of support stretches all across our amazing state, from Oakland to Ocean City— and everywhere in between. Together we will achieve our vision of expanding jobs, justice, and opportunity for all Marylanders. Cheers, Team Tom On the Campaign Trail Tom kicked off last weekend at Open Works in Baltimore with our friend Senator Cory McCray and dozens of other leaders. We cannot have a thriving Maryland without a thriving Baltimore, and Team Perez-Sneed is determined in creating a state that works for all — no matter your zip code. The energy at our Prince George’s County on Saturday afternoon was incredible. Thank you to Senator Joanne Benson, Delegates Veronica Turner and Anne Healey, and countless others who braved the heat to kick off the opening of our new office in gorgeous Prince George’s. As always, Tom was glad to be surrounded by great people. Special thanks to members of CASA in Action, IBEW Local 26, AFSCME, SEIU, UFCW, and more for stopping by and for your continued support of our vision. On Sunday, Tom and Shannon were delighted to join activists for the Montgomery County Democratic Central Committee Spring Gala. Together, we will make sure that our state is all blue in 2022! Later that day, they joined former Maryland Democratic Party Chair Kathleen Matthews for an event at her home. Kathleen is a dedicated activist and leader, and we are so grateful for her support. As a Maryland Emerge alumna and sister herself, Shannon was honored that President of Emerge America, Ashanti Gholar, also joined. #TeamPerezSneed was fired up and ready for change last night at the Maryland Democratic Party's Annual Gala in Upper Marlboro. Tom and Shannon had a great evening with a room full of Democrats where they enjoyed reconnecting with friends, old and new — including the inspirational United States Senator Cory Booker! subject: There’s too much at stake for me to lose my election again

body:
#

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mek-em-hassan-may22?refcode=em220527-2-7&t=1&refcode2=2916_6688874_RSSPDC&akid=2916%2E6688874%2ERSSPDC)
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mek-em-hassan-may22?refcode=em220527-2-7&t=2&refcode2=2916_6688874_RSSPDC&akid=2916%2E6688874%2ERSSPDC)**

Hello,
I lost the very first election I ran in. It was 2002, and I lost my New Hampshire State Senate race.
I didn’t let that loss deter me — just like I don’t let Republican attacks deter me now.
**Let me be clear, because there is so much at stake: We cannot lose this seat. Not this time. Not with _Roe v. Wade_ hanging on by a thread.**
**But Rachel Maddow said I have a difficult reelection fight ahead of me, and a recent poll shows me down by two points to an extreme anti-choice opponent.**
I ran for office to make a difference for as many people who needed my help as I could and to ensure that every American has the opportunity to succeed, no matter who they are.
My 2002 and 2004 elections are well in the rearview mirror. Today, the stakes are so much higher. And alarmingly, a recent poll shows me down by two points.
**If we lose this seat, Democrats forfeit Senate control to Mitch McConnell who, just a couple of days ago, suggested that if he’s in charge we could be heading for a national abortion ban.**
I’m emailing today, everyone, because I need your help.
[**Will you please split a grassroots donation — $3 or any amount you can — between my campaign and Mark Kelly’s before our end-of-month deadline to hold our seats and control of the Senate?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mek-em-hassan-may22?refcode=em220527-2-7&t=3&refcode2=2916_6688874_RSSPDC&akid=2916%2E6688874%2ERSSPDC)
Winning and preserving our most basic fundamental rights truly takes all of us coming together, and I’m counting on you. Thank you for getting involved.
With every good wish,
Maggie Hassan

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you want to, you can [ unsubscribe here](https://act.markkelly.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=4&akid=2916%2E6688874%2ERSSPDC).
Mark Kelly was a Captain in the U.S. Navy and astronaut. body:
As with any tragedy, Democrats are moving quickly to further their agenda to disarm law-abiding citizens.
****

Patriot,

We are all heartbroken over the 21 lives lost in Uvalde, Texas.

As with any tragedy, Democrats are moving quickly to further their agenda to disarm law-abiding citizens.

Nancy Pelosi's Second-in-Command, Steny Hoyer, has re-introduced legislation that would take Red Flag laws to a new level in his, "Federal Extreme Risk Protection Order Act."

And even Republicans, succumbing to public pressure, are going right along with it.

Mitch McConnell even commented on the Red Flag bill saying, "What we can't do is fail to pass something."

**He 's wrong!**

What we can't do is create illogical and reactionary "solutions" to gun violence that will leave innocent Americans defenseless!

Guns aren't the issue here.

**Parenting is the issue! Mental illness is the issue! Leftism, which separates morality from society, is the issue!**

Gun violence, especially school shootings, **stops IN THE HOME!**

And we need to elect leaders bold enough to say that!

That's why I ask that you help me become one of those leaders [by supporting my congressional campaign today.](https://libersend.lauraloomerforcongress.com/l/jaHkxHkvgw3mMH3vyc0Hsw/6lS6ZuL42DZyicTa7Gsj892Q/Zb7A763yrh2Z5B5iY7r5d17A)

America needs a wakeup call. And that takes leadership that is willing to weather the abuse from the Left, the fake news media, and boldly say these unpopular truths, even in our toughest times.

_Image courtesy WBIR_ A few months ago, I told you about the experience I had joining the organization Mobile Meals Kitchen (a group feeding our seniors for 50 years) to help deliver food, support, and safety checks to 1,200 senior citizens in need here in Knox County. This week I got to revisit these fantastic folks at Mobile Meals Kitchen to celebrate their facility’s expansion and upgrade to serve even more people in the community. _**"I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [Herschel Walker and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."**
--Elie Mystal, MSNBC_

Fellow American,

I recently wrote to you about a racist article attacking me in _The Nation_.

The author had some pretty heinous things to say because I'm a Black conservative. You may recall this line:

_"Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people."_
Well, Fellow American, he's back at it again. MSNBC featured this man on their network this week so he could spew even more anti-Black, anti-conservative vitriol in the name of mediocre TV ratings.

_"I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [referring to me and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."_
**That's racist, disgusting, and sad.**

I never wanted the color of my skin to be a focal point of this Senate campaign, but these attacks on my character and my skin color have gone too far.

**You can help me prove them wrong by standing with me at this critical moment.**

| | Al entrar en este fin de semana del Día Memorial, los acontecimientos de los antepasados ponen de manifiesto lo que hizo grande a este país. Los fundadores crearon un nuevo país basado en los derechos inalienables a la vida, la libertad y la búsqueda de la felicidad. Fuimos a la guerra y se derramó sangre para hacerlo realidad. La Constitución dejó claro que el derecho a la privacidad en nuestros hogares y cuerpos merecía protección, limitó la intervención del gobierno y garantizó que el estado de derecho y no las creencias religiosas impedirían otras interpretaciones. | | Peter, **This week, our country endured another mass shooting in a public school.** Uvalde. Parkland. Sandy Hook. Columbine. These names are seared into our collective memories. Unspeakable tragedies that devastated communities and stole away the lives of children and educators. May 21st of this year - just last week - was the 24th anniversary of the shooting at Thurston High School here in Springfield, where I live. It was shocking. It was unthinkable. And in the 24 years since, it has become all too normalized in our society to have children murdered in their classroom. It's hard to know what to say in these moments, but I do know this: **We cannot treat these tragedies as inevitable. We cannot treat them as normal. We cannot treat them as unpreventable.** And we need leaders in Congress who are willing to stand up to the gun lobby and pass common sense gun safety legislation that will save lives. We have proven solutions to the gun violence epidemic. Here in Oregon, I was proud to lead the passage of our universal background checks law. We've passed legislation to keep guns out of the hands of domestic abusers, and to prevent people who are experiencing a mental health crisis from accessing a firearm. Peter, I'm tired. I'm tired of seeing our nation mourn for the victims of mass shootings. Tired of offering thoughts and prayers while more children die. Tired of teachers having to spend their time training children how to avoid being murdered by an active shooter. Tired of children thinking this is normal. And I'm tired of waiting for Congress to stand up to the gun lobby on behalf of our communities and our children. **Enough is enough.** When I'm in Congress, gun violence prevention will be a priority. I've taken on the gun lobby before, and I'll do it again. Thanks for standing with me, _Val_ |

clean_body: | | | Peter, This week, our country endured another mass shooting in a public school. Uvalde. Parkland. Sandy Hook. Columbine. These names are seared into our collective memories. Unspeakable tragedies that devastated communities and stole away the lives of children and educators. May 21st of this year - just last week - was the 24th anniversary of the shooting at Thurston High School here in Springfield, where I live. It was shocking. It was unthinkable. And in the 24 years since, it has become all too normalized in our society to have children murdered in their classroom. It's hard to know what to say in these moments, but I do know this: We cannot treat these tragedies as inevitable. We cannot treat them as normal. We cannot treat them as unpreventable. And we need leaders in Congress who are willing to stand up to the gun lobby and pass common sense gun safety legislation that will save lives. We have proven solutions to the gun violence epidemic. Here in Oregon, I was proud to lead the passage of our universal background checks law. We've passed legislation to keep guns out of the hands of domestic abusers, and to prevent people who are experiencing a mental health crisis from accessing a firearm. Peter, I'm tired. I'm tired of seeing our nation mourn for the victims of mass shootings. Tired of offering thoughts and prayers while more children die. Tired of teachers having to spend their time training children how to avoid being murdered by an active shooter. Tired of children thinking this is normal. And I'm tired of waiting for Congress to stand up to the gun lobby on behalf of our communities and our children. Enough is enough. When I'm in Congress, gun violence prevention will be a priority. I've taken on the gun lobby before, and I'll do it again. Dear - ** ** I wanted to reshare with you this email I sent last week. ** ** Just last week, I did what I have done too many times. I shared my heartfelt condolences to family members, friends, and an entire community who experienced the violent wrath of white supremacy and gun violence. And as I have done after each senseless mass shooting we've seen in the news, I called and pleaded for common-sense gun reform. ** ** Now, the cycle has already repeated, this time with innocent, precious elementary school children. I refuse to sit idly by as our leaders continue to put the gun lobby above our children, teachers, churchgoers, grocery shoppers- innocent people time after time. Nothing, absolutely nothing, will change unless we vote out the complacent elected officials whose inaction fuels this crisis, starting with Governor McMaster. ** ** Mass shootings at schools, malls, grocery stores, and churches are totally foreseeable, absolutely probable and a direct result of the choices Republican governors like Greg Abbott in TX and Henry McMaster in SC make, along with their Republican legislative colleagues. ** ** As South Carolina's next Governor, I will continue to do everything in my power to protect our children and curb the rising tide of gun violence through common sense gun reforms that bring our communities and government leaders together to create a better, stronger, safer South Carolina...for all of us. ** ** It's critical that we send a clear signal on June 14th-that we will no longer stand by while innocent lives are being taken because our leaders lack the political courage to take action. Together, we will take action, but we will not get there without your help. Early voting runs from May 31st to June 10th with no excuse. It's time to make your voice heard and send a strong message to Governor McMaster that his failed leadership on this issue, and so many others, will no longer be tolerated. ** ** Thank you for your continued support, Mia
---
|
---
FORWARDED MESSAGE: , It's taken me a bit to process the tragedy that took place last weekend in Buffalo, New York, but I knew I wanted to share my thoughts with you. It's heartbreaking that still in America, Black people are going about their everyday lives, only to die at the hands of a white supremacist who targeted them because of their skin color. ** ** Substitute a grocery store in Buffalo with a church in Charleston and the parallels between the tragedies are striking. As I'm sure it did for many of you, hearing the news brought me straight back to that horrible June day in 2015. I was flooded with the fear, the frustration, and the worry that despite my best efforts, our lawmakers will do largely nothing to prevent the next act of targeted racial violence. ** ** Unfortunately, it looks like my concerns are justified: South Carolina Republicans just last week, minutes before the legislative session ended, blocked the passage of the Clementa C. Pinckney Hate Crimes Act. This legislation, named in honor of my former colleague and our late State Senator who was tragically murdered at the Mother Emanuel AME Church, would increase the criminal penalty for crimes motivated by hatred of a victim based on race, ethnicity, religion, or other unchangeable features. Legislative session after legislative session, I've fought tooth and nail for this bill. As hate crimes are on the rise, it was infuriating to see the Republicans block this bill again, making South Carolina one of just two states without a hate crimes law. ** ** How can Republicans continue to justify their unbridled hypocrisy? They refuse to pass the most basic common-sense gun reforms that would save lives. They refuse to pass a hate crimes law. They've shredded our social safety net, making it harder for South Carolina families to make ends meet. And they do all of this under the guise of being pro-life- now how does that make a lick of sense? ** ** In times like these, when the news is so gut-wrenching, I know it can be tempting to disengage from politics, but we can't fall into that trap. We have to do something. ** ** All McMaster and the GOP have to offer is empty thoughts and silent prayers, and I've had enough. South Carolinians need an advocate who will stand up for common-sense gun legislation and stand up against hate crimes- that's why I'm running against McMaster for Governor- because South Carolina deserves better. ** ** In solidarity, Mia
---
About Senator Mia McLeod: Senator Mia McLeod is a working mom, small business owner, and seventh-generation South Carolinian from Bennettsville, South Carolina. She is a former State Representative, current State Senator representing District 22, and is running as a Democratic candidate for Governor.

How can Republicans continue to justify their unbridled hypocrisy? They refuse to pass the most basic common-sense gun reforms that would save lives. They refuse to pass a hate crimes law. They've shredded our social safety net, making it harder for South Carolina families to make ends meet. And they do all of this under the guise of being pro-life- now how does that make a lick of sense? In times like these, when the news is so gut-wrenching, I know it can be tempting to disengage from politics, but we can't fall into that trap. We have to do something. All McMaster and the GOP have to offer is empty thoughts and silent prayers, and I've had enough. South Carolinians need an advocate who will stand up for common-sense gun legislation and stand up against hate crimes- that's why I'm running against McMaster for Governor- because South Carolina deserves better. In solidarity, Mia About Senator Mia McLeod: Senator Mia McLeod is a working mom, small business owner, and seventh-generation South Carolinian from Bennettsville, South Carolina. * * *
**Issue Spotlight: Administrative Rules Reform
** As the law stands in Illinois right now, any rule that is put out by the Illinois administrative agencies has a presumption of legality. After the public has the opportunity to comment, the rule automatically becomes law unless 8 out of 12 members on the Joint Committee for Administrative Rules (JCAR) vote to strike it down. One of the pillars of our "A New Start for Illinois" policy agenda is a fundamental change to this process. We are proposing that "emergency" rules and rules that raise fees/penalties shall not become effective unless they receive seven YES votes from JCAR members. This is a necessary first step in reining in the executive branch of Illinois government.
Thank you for reading and please remember to honor our fallen this holiday weekend. Semper Fidelis, Paul

The truth is, I never planned to run for public office. But when Scott Walker tried to consolidate power and get rid of the State Treasurer’s office — a critical check and balance on our government — I knew something had to be done.

So, as a political nobody, I stepped up and took on the most powerful Republican in Wisconsin. I led a statewide grassroots effort to stop Walker’s power grab, and we won with 62% of the vote. It was a landslide victory.

Shortly after, I decided to run for State Treasurer and won my second statewide election — flipping nine Trump counties and winning by a larger margin than the Governor, Lt. Governor, and Attorney General. (Heck, I even flipped Ron Johnson’s home county!)

Look, I didn’t run for public office for fame, money, or power. I first ran because I believed the people of Wisconsin deserved to have someone fighting for them, not bending to the will of wealthy donors and corporate interests.

Now I'm running for the U.S. Senate because I'm frustrated by the influence of corporate money in our politics. I'm fed up with Ron Johnson’s refusal to help the people who elected him. And I'm sick and tired of watching our 50/50 Senate majority get blocked by a minority of Republicans at every possible turn.

When I’m in the U.S. Senate, I’ll fight like hell to lower everyday costs for families, protect our democracy, defend reproductive freedom, bring down prescription drug costs, pass critical gun safety legislation — and end the filibuster if that’s what it takes to get it all done.

I’m not taking a dime of corporate PAC money, which means I'm counting on the continued support of this grassroots team to help fund our campaign and help us defeat Ron Johnson.
